function_question: How does nature sense messages without hearing?

opening.text: There was a boy called Jonah whose grandpa told the best stories and grew the biggest tomatoes on the street.
After school, Jonah visited Grandpa, and they worked in the garden together. Grandpa's ears weren't as sharp as they used to be, but his jokes were.
Grandpa's best friend came to visit and rang and rang the bell. Grandpa was in the garden and never heard it. "I missed him," Grandpa said sadly. "I wish I could feel the doorbell."

card.problem: Grandpa is hard of hearing and misses visitors at the door
card.goal: Design a signal he can feel or see anywhere in the house
card.rules: It must work in 4 rooms, with safe low-voltage parts only

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The missed visitor
chapters.line: Jonah wonders: how can Grandpa know someone is at the door without hearing the bell?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Jonah needs a teammate
chapters.line: Grandpa deserves two kind inventors. Will you join Jonah?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The silent messengers
chapters.line: You and Jonah meet heroes that send messages with shakes, ripples and light.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the channel
chapters.line: The heroes share how to send a message a different way.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The secret signal game
chapters.line: Jonah closes his eyes, plugs his ears and waits for a signal.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: Kind, useful feedback
chapters.line: Three magic sentence starters help you make your design better.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The signal map
chapters.line: Every good signal starts with a map of where it needs to go.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: Grandpa tries it
chapters.line: The first signal misses the garden. You listen to Grandpa's feedback and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Tea with a friend
chapters.line: Grandpa feels the signal and opens the door with a big smile.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Jonah's grandpa is hard of hearing and keeps missing visitors at the door. He needs a signal he can feel or see in every room. Can you help Jonah? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some inventors already have a spark of an idea for a signal without sound. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Lots of animals send messages without any sound at all. Tap each card to meet four silent messengers!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which signal will your partner notice most with their eyes closed and ears covered?
guide.sketch: Time to draw a map of Grandpa's house and show where your signal travels!
guide.build_and_test: Build your signal, test it in 4 rooms, then let Grandpa try it. The real user is the best tester!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Pick ONE thing from your user's feedback, change it and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Grandpa never misses a visitor. When someone rings, your signal finds him in every room, even among the tomatoes!

quick_check.question: Jonah tests his signal in Grandpa's 4 rooms. Grandpa notices it in 3 of them. What fraction of the rooms does it work in?
quick_check.right: Right! 3 out of 4 rooms is 3/4, which is 75%. One more room to go!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Put the rooms it works in on top and all the rooms underneath.

clue_cards.name: Elephant
clue_cards.trick: Touch sensors in its feet and trunk feel rumbles in the ground.
clue_cards.does: It picks up messages from other elephants several kilometres away.

clue_cards.name: Sand scorpion
clue_cards.trick: Sensors on its eight legs feel tiny ripples in the sand.
clue_cards.does: It finds a beetle's footsteps from about 50 cm away, in the dark.

clue_cards.name: Spider
clue_cards.trick: Its legs feel every shake that travels along the silk.
clue_cards.does: It can tell a trapped fly from the wind or a visiting spider.

clue_cards.name: Firefly
clue_cards.trick: It flashes its own light pattern, like a secret code.
clue_cards.does: Others of its kind see the code and find it in the dark.

predict.prompt: Do you feel it or see it? Predict first!

items.label: A phone buzzing in your pocket

predict.explain: The same message can travel through different channels. Deaf and hard-of-hearing people often use doorbells that flash lights and alarms that shake the bed: same message, new channel.

lab.title: The secret signal game
lab.predict: Your partner closes their eyes and covers their ears. Which signal will they notice most often out of 5 tries?
options: Tug a string on the wrist

tool.name: I Like, I Wish, What If
tool.intro: I Like, I Wish, What If is a way to give kind, useful feedback on a prototype. You can ask a friend, your user, or yourself. Today you'll learn all 3 parts.

parts.name: I like…
parts.what: Say one thing that works well.
parts.example: ✈️ I like how straight it flies.

parts.name: I wish…
parts.what: Say one thing that could be better, kindly.
parts.example: ✈️ I wish it didn't dive down at the end.
parts.starter: I wish Grandpa could notice it when he's…

parts.name: What if…?
parts.what: Share a new idea to try.
parts.example: ✈️ What if we folded the wing tips up a little?

sketch_checklist: I drew a map of the house with the front door and 4 rooms.
I showed how my signal travels to each room.
I labelled the channel: vibration, light or movement.

test.measure: rooms where the signal is noticed (out of 4)
test.check_question: User check: who tested your signal?
check_options: Only me, with ear defenders on

reflection.question: Which nature trick helped your signal most?
